title: Tens All Round: Portugal Hands Out Double Figures, Williams Takes the Trophy by 12
title_candidates: Tens All Round: Portugal Hands Out Double Figures, Williams Takes the Trophy by 12
Six Men, Three New Courses, Seven Double Figures: Williams Bleeds Least and Wins by 12
The Cascais Carnage: Williams Wins Wire-to-Wire, Mullin Reclaims the Jacket at the Second Hole
Absorb and Survive: How Gregg Williams Made Two 10s and Still Won by 12
theme: Three brand-new Portuguese courses spent four rounds handing out double figures to every single player in the field — TEG 8 was won not by the man who played best but by the man whose disasters cost him least, and Gregg Williams's disasters cost him nothing at all.
tone: house — faithful, entertaining, tongue-in-cheek; Ronay/Peck register, dry rather than zany, every joke anchored to a scorecard
opening_hook: Open on the arithmetic of destruction rather than the leaderboard: the double-figure holes strewn across Quinta da Marinha, Penha Longa and Oitavos Dunes (b46, b09, b10, b08, b23, b06, b19) — every one of the six men signed for at least one blow-up — then ask the only question that mattered, which was who could absorb them, and answer it: Williams, by 12.
foreshadow: Williams comes in with two Trophies and a Green Jacket rank of exactly 5th in each of the last three TEGs — a man who has never once threatened a gross prize.
Alex Baker arrives as the reigning Wooden Spoon holder, last of six on both counts in TEG 7 — and opens TEG 8 with five straight bogeys.
Mullin arrives on five Jackets and back-to-back wins; the gross lead looks his by default until a Baker starts posting numbers on the same card.
Neumann has finished 3rd on the Trophy in each of the last three TEGs and has never held a Spoon — a record that lasts until the fourth hole of the tournament.

competitions.name: Trophy (Stableford)
competitions.how: Williams took the outright lead at R1 H10 during a 14-point burst across holes 8-11 (b12), closed R1 on 38 pts and four clear, then produced 41 at Penha Longa — including a 10 at the 12th (b09) — to stretch the cushion to 11. A 29-point R3 at Quinta da Marinha, with a 10 at the 11th (b10) inside a 14-shot bleed across 8-11 (b35), cut the lead to 5 and was the only wobble of the tournament; Oitavos Dunes then produced another 41, with 12 points in four holes from the 12th (b11) after an 11-shot bleed from the 5th (b34). Final: 149 pts, by 12 over Alex Baker (b02) — wire-to-wire, no lead change after R1, a third Trophy.

competitions.name: Green Jacket (Gross)
competitions.how: Mullin had the outright gross lead from R1 H13 and stood 6 clear after the lowest round of the tournament, an 86 at Penha Longa (+14). Then Quinta da Marinha's second visit undid him: his worst round to date (b17, 26 pts / +26) let Jon Baker — round of 89, the best gross figure posted on that course — take the lead at R3 H13 after 36 holes of Mullin in front (b01). Two holes into Oitavos Dunes, a bogey at the 2nd was enough to take it straight back (b03), the one lead change of the tournament flagged decisive; +17 on the links closed it out at +77, by 6 (b05). Six Jackets, three in a row.

competitions.name: Wooden Spoon
competitions.how: Settled almost before it began. Neumann was bottom of the pile at R1 H1, briefly reprieved when Meller made a 10 at the 3rd (b80), and back at the bottom at H4 — where he stayed for all 72 holes. Holes 7-15 of R1 cost him 29 shots (b04), including nines at the 10th, 11th and 12th, and produced his worst round to date on both metrics (17 pts, +43: b32, b33). R3 repeated the trick — a 10 at the 1st (b23) inside a 17-shot opening five (b36) and an 11 at the 10th (b08). Rounds of 31 and 32 on the two new courses were respectable and irrelevant: 100 pts, last by a distance (b18), and a first Spoon for a man who had been 3rd on the Trophy three TEGs running.

rounds.angle: Portugal's most punishing layout, and the leaderboard barely notices: Williams runs up a 10 at the par-5 12th (b09) and still signs for 41 pts to go 11 clear, while Mullin's 86 (+14) — the lowest gross round anyone managed all tournament — pushes his Jacket cushion to six and Neumann's 9 at the SI-1 16th (b22) keeps his afternoon on brand.

rounds.chosen_headline: Baker Steals the Jacket as Marinha Feasts on Everyone Else
rounds.angle: The tournament's only repeat course collects its dues: Mullin's worst round to date (b17) hands Jon Baker the gross lead at the 13th after 36 holes in front (b01); Williams bleeds 14 shots from the 8th including a 10 at the 11th (b10, b35) and sees his Trophy lead cut from 11 to 5; Alex Baker makes a 10 at the SI-1 8th (b06) and Neumann a 10 at the 1st and an 11 at the 10th (b23, b36, b08).

headline_candidates: Two Holes In, Mullin Has the Jacket Back
41 on the Dunes: Williams Closes Out by 12

rounds.chosen_headline: Two Holes In, Mullin Has the Jacket Back — and Williams Has the Trophy by 12
rounds.angle: Oitavos Dunes settles all three: a bogey at the 2nd is enough for Mullin to reclaim the gross lead outright (b03) and win by 6 (b05); Meller drops 22 shots in the first six holes with a 10 at the 4th (b07, b19); Williams bleeds 11 from the 5th (b34), then answers with 12 points in four holes from the 12th (b11) for 41 and a 12-point win (b02); Alex Baker signs off with a 9 at the SI-2 18th (b16) and is runner-up regardless, with Neumann's 32 leaving him bottom for the fourth time in four rounds (b18).

players.arc: Two prior Trophies and a Jacket rank of exactly 5th in each of the last three TEGs — and here the handicap sheet does its work perfectly: outright leader from R1 H10 to the final putt, two 10s (b09, b10) and a 29-point R3 absorbed without ever being caught, 149 pts and a third Trophy by 12 (b02).

Five Jackets and back-to-back wins going in, and he makes it six and three in a row (b05) — but only after his worst round to date at Quinta da Marinha (b17) let Jon Baker strip him of a lead he had held for 36 holes (b01), and only by taking it straight back two holes into Oitavos (b03).

One prior Trophy and gross runner-up in TEG 5 and 6; his 89 in R3 was the best gross round anyone posted at Quinta da Marinha and put him two clear of Mullin (b01), but a quintuple bogey at the 13th in R1 and a links finish left him second in gross again, 6 back.

The reigning Wooden Spoon holder, last of six on both counts in TEG 7, opens with 15 points in five holes (b13) and finishes Trophy runner-up — despite a 10 at the SI-1 8th in R3 (b06) and a 9 at the SI-2 last in R4 (b16), which is one way to spend a promotion.

Third on the Trophy in each of the last three TEGs and never a Spoon holder — until the fourth hole of R1, after which he was bottom at every single checkpoint: 29 shots gone in nine holes (b04), a worst-ever round on both metrics (b32, b33), a 10 and an 11 in R3 (b23, b08), 100 pts and the Spoon (b18).

Defending Trophy champion with three prior Spoons on the CV; a 10 at the 3rd in R1 briefly deposited him at the bottom of the Spoon race (b46, b80), and 22 shots in the opening six at Oitavos, a 10 at the 4th included (b07, b19), ensured the defence never got going.

venue_notes: TEG's 2nd visit to the Lisbon Coast, November 2015, and every one of the three courses was new to TEG — no form, no local knowledge, no excuses that hadn't been invented yet. Use Quinta da Marinha (R1 and R3, the only repeat, Robert Trent Jones Sr., elevated targets and abundant bunkering inside a private pine estate at Cascais) as the venue villain: it produced the tournament's worst rounds and the Jacket lead change. Note the father-and-son back-to-back — RTJ Sr. at Marinha, then RTJ Jr.'s Atlantic Course at Penha Longa in the Sintra hills, steep, dramatic and reputedly Portugal's most testing layout, which nonetheless yielded Mullin's 86 and Williams's 41 pts. Save Oitavos Dunes for the resolution: a pure Arthur Hills links on the Atlantic, host of multiple Portuguese Opens, where two holes decided the Jacket and Meller lost 22 shots in six.
course_history_notes: All three venues were new to TEG in 2015, so nobody had prior course form to lean on — Quinta da Marinha was the only course played twice (R1 and R3).
Mullin's 86 (+14) at Penha Longa in R2 was the lowest gross round posted by anyone on any of the three courses.
Jon Baker's 89 at Quinta da Marinha in R3 was the best gross round anyone managed there, and it was worth the Green Jacket lead for one round.
Neumann's 114 at Quinta da Marinha in R1 (+43) was his worst gross round in TEG history to date (b33).
decisive_moments: Trophy: R2 at Penha Longa — Williams signs for 41 pts despite a 10 at the 12th (b09) and stretches the lead from 4 to 11; the Trophy is never genuinely contested again, the R3 dip to 5 notwithstanding.

Green Jacket: R4 H2 at Oitavos Dunes — a bogey at the 2nd is enough for Mullin to take the gross lead back off Jon Baker outright (b03), the one lead change of the tournament rated decisive; he wins by 6.

Wooden Spoon: R1 H4 at Quinta da Marinha — Neumann returns to the bottom of the field and stays there for the remaining 68 holes, the 29-shot bleed across holes 7-15 (b04) making it unrecoverable by lunchtime on the first day.

payoffs.payoff: He wins the Trophy for a third time on 149 pts by 12 (b02) while never appearing in the Jacket conversation: the split is ordinary handicapping, and it is exactly how he wins.

payoffs.seed: Alex Baker arrives as reigning Wooden Spoon holder
payoffs.payoff: He finishes Trophy runner-up, having made a 10 at the SI-1 8th in R3 (b06) and a 9 at the SI-2 18th in R4 (b16) — promotion earned the hard way, and the Spoon passes to Neumann (b18).

payoffs.seed: Mullin's Jacket looks his by default
payoffs.payoff: Jon Baker takes it at R3 H13 after 36 holes of Mullin in front (b01) following Mullin's worst round to date (b17); Mullin reclaims it at R4 H2 (b03) and wins by 6 (b05).

payoffs.seed: Neumann: 3rd on the Trophy three TEGs running, no Spoon on the CV
payoffs.resolves_in: How the three were decided — Wooden Spoon
payoffs.payoff: Bottom from R1 H4 onwards, 29 shots gone in nine holes (b04), worst-ever round on both metrics (b32, b33), and a first Wooden Spoon on 100 pts (b18).

vehicle_fit_response.note: b01, b04 and b34 are all real, but nobody's collapse decided anything — Williams led wire-to-wire and won by 12 — so the collapses are the texture, not the frame: the story is the whole field being mauled by three new Portuguese courses, which is ensemble plus a catalogue of double figures, with the procession as supporting inevitability.
